description: Excavations between 2013 and 2019 at the junction of the A1, A241, and the River Great Ouse ahead of the construction of a quarry revealed a rectangular structure interpreted as an Iron Age Shrine. Little information about the dating of the site is immediately available, bit comparisons are made to Late Iron Age sites such as Hayling Island, and would appear to fit in well with other middle to late Iron age shrine sites.
bibliography: Current Archaeology. “The Archaeology of Black Cat Quarry - Farming, Flooding, and Fighting in the Great Ouse Valley.” 2022. https://the-past.com/feature/the-archaeology-of-black-cat-quarry-farming-flooding-and-fighting-in-the-great-ouse-valley/.
